svg.title: Rectangular fabric grids with two-centimetre edge margins
svg.desc: Two diagrams at the same scale show a 140 by 100 centimetre fabric rectangle with a two-centimetre margin on all four edges, leaving 136 by 96 centimetres usable. The original 20 by 30 centimetre grid fits eighteen pieces. Turning every piece gives a 30 by 20 centimetre grid fitting sixteen. All gaps are zero. These two grids do not establish an optimal mixed layout. AI-assisted programmatic authorship by Sewlore. No physical testing was performed.

svg.text: Fabric: 140 × 100 cm · Cutting pieces: 20 × 30 cm · Each edge margin: 2 cm · Gap: 0
Usable: 136 × 96 cm. Unfilled usable space stays visible.
Turn pieces only when grain, nap and print permit it.
across = floor((usable width + gap) / (piece width + gap)); rows use the same rule.
count = across × rows. This compares two uniform grids; it is not optimal mixed nesting.
Hypothetical example. Prepared by Sewlore with AI-assisted programmatic drawing.
